Atom economy is a measure of how efficiently the atoms of the reactants are used to produce the desired product in a chemical reaction. In some chemical reactions, more than one product is formed. One product may be useful while the others may be unwanted byproducts. A reaction with a high atom economy uses a large proportion of the reactant atoms to make the desired product. A reaction with a low atom economy produces a greater proportion of unwanted byproducts. Atom economy is particularly important in industrial chemistry because it helps manufacturers reduce waste and use raw materials more efficiently. How do we calculate atom economy? We use the following formula. Atom economy equals the relative formula mass of the desired product taking account of its coefficient in the balanced equation divided by the total relative formula mass of all products also taking account of their coefficients multiplied by 100.
